# nav-progress — deliverable

**Commit on main:** `574d871ca` feat(web): show a navigation-pending bar while a route loads (fast-forward on `819b43229`). Build kept: `chainglass-nav-progress/apps/web/.next` BUILD_ID `H6HI76hQQhvLuy720tKTm` (built by the fft run on this head).

## Approach (and why)
The App Router has no global navigation events, and Next 16's `useRouter()` returns a per-component memoized copy of `push`/`replace` (checked in `next/dist/client/components/navigation.js`), so patching the router singleton is fragile. The boring option taken:
- **Start, links:** one capture-phase `document` click listener in `NavigationProgress` treats a plain left click on an in-app `<a href>` (every Next `<Link>` renders one) that would change pathname or search as a navigation start. Ignored: same URL, hash-only, other origin, `target` other than `_self`, `download`, modifier keys, non-left button.
- **Start, programmatic:** `useProgressRouter()` = `useRouter()` whose `push`/`replace` announce the start first. Swapped in at all 8 `router.push`/`replace` call sites: worktree switch (`browser-client.tsx`), mobile tab bar (`bottom-tab-bar.tsx`), `sdk:navigate` (`sdk-provider.tsx`), pij rail toggle, terminal path links, workflow creation, work-unit creation, terminal mobile redirect. Prime approved the shared-file edits.
- **End:** `usePathname()` + `useSearchParams()` change (the router rendered the new URL).
- **Show delay** 150 ms (instant navigations never flash); **give up** after 20 s if the URL never changes (a handler cancelling a `<Link>`, a failed fetch).
- **Look:** 3px sky bar on the bottom edge (Jordan: "something along the bottom"), a segment sweeping across a faint track; fixed, `pointer-events-none`, no layout shift; reads on light and dark; reduced motion = static full bar. Rendered as `<output>` with sr-only "Loading page" so screen readers announce it.
- **Mount:** once in `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` inside `<Suspense fallback={null}>` (needed for `useSearchParams`). Did not touch `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` or `workspaces/[slug]/layout.tsx`. No `loading.tsx` added.
- Concept search first (scout): no existing indicator, nprogress, top loader, `useLinkStatus` or navigation `useTransition` in the repo.

## Acceptance evidence
- **Unit test** `test/unit/web/components/navigation/navigation-progress.test.tsx` (4): appears only after the delay on a link click and hides on pathname change; covers a `router.push` that only changes the query (worktree switch); never shows for a navigation that renders inside the delay; never shows for a same-URL click, a `target=_blank` link, or a modified click.
- **Browser proof** on my prod build at :3108 (private tmux, no sidecar; RSC responses delayed 3 s by request interception so mid-navigation is capturable): bar visible mid-navigation, gone after the route rendered:
  - into a workspace (home → Chainglass card): `scratch/nav-progress-workspace-light.png`, `scratch/nav-progress-workspace-dark.png`
  - branch switch (worktree switcher → another worktree): `scratch/nav-progress-branch-light.png`, `scratch/nav-progress-branch-dark.png`
  (in `/Users/jordanknight/substrate/chainglass/scratch/`). No console errors. Under load ~130, the bar appeared ~390 ms after the click instead of the 150 ms target (main thread busy); once, during the light branch switch, it wasn't up yet at the 700 ms check.
- **just fft** (nice -n 19, worktree, rebased on `819b43229`, 16:01–16:10, load 38.5 at start → 48.6 at end): lint clean (1808 files); build 7/7; typecheck all 9 configs clean; vitest 553 files / 7309 tests passed (7 files / 60 skipped, existing), including the 4 new tests; `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` 0 high (3 low, 16 moderate). Build warnings are in untouched code (Turbopack whole-project trace from `remote-view-service.production.ts:252`, `workflow/dist/resolvers/git-worktree.resolver.js:122`, `workflow/dist/services/workflow.service.js:233`; CLI esbuild `import.meta` in cjs). Full log: `/tmp/nav-progress-fft.log` (4306 lines). The brief sets no before/after timing for this item: the bar shows a navigation is happening but doesn't make it faster.
